faqs.q: What experience does your company have in providing online samples for market research? How long have you been providing this service? Do you also provide similar services for other uses such as direct marketing? If so, what proportion of your work is for market research?
faqs.a: Our company was founded in 2017 and started the online portals www.turn2opinion.com, www.myfrequentrewards.com and www.myhealthopinions.com. After creating our in-house panel, our company has completed more than 23,500 online studies for clients around the globe, with over 3.43M consumer panellists, 2.85M business panellists and almost 1.5M healthcare profiles. Our B2B proprietary panel site carries respondents from 40+ geographies including the USA, Canada, Mexico, UK, Spain, Italy, Australia, France, Germany, India, China, Japan, Singapore, Brazil, Turkey, Russia and Malaysia, among many others. We are constantly working to grow our consumer panel in all geographies and to add new markets to our offering. We conduct over 100,000 interviews every year around the globe among consumers and B2B professionals. Our proprietary panel of engaged survey respondents, together with our recruitment sources, allows our team to provide global reach representing over 95 geographies including vendor partners. During the research process, data is collected from participants and statistical analysis or qualitative assessment is conducted to draw meaningful insights and conclusions. These insights help organisations make informed decisions about their products, services, marketing strategies and other aspects of their business. We do not use our panel for any other marketing promotion. Our audience is used for market research purposes only.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you have staff with responsibility for developing and monitoring the performance of the sampling algorithms and related automated functions who also have knowledge and experience in this area? What sort of training in sampling techniques do you provide to your frontline staff?
faqs.a: Since 2017 we have had an in-house panel management and supply team to manage all sample supply and panellist registration. We also have an in-house QA recruitment team who analyse and allow only valid users to be registered on our panel. The team applies qualitative and quantitative measures to analyse real-time responses and generate a quality score, and monitors whole fieldwork progress and respondent participation history. Each team member is trained on our recruitment algorithm and validations so that only the right user can enter, samples are correctly diversified with verified demographics, and our panel databases hold individuals who have agreed to participate in surveys, studies or research projects. Our panel is built through various methods, including opt-in registrations, partnerships and recruitment through online advertisements. Once a research project is initiated, our team selects a sample from the database that matches the desired target audience based on specific demographics, characteristics or criteria, using screening questions to ensure participants meet the study requirements. Selected individuals are then invited to participate, usually through online surveys or other digital methods. We also employ techniques such as random sampling or quota sampling to minimise bias and ensure a more accurate representation of the target population.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What other services do you offer? Do you cover sample-only, or do you offer a broad range of data collection and analysis services?
faqs.a: Our offering includes programming and hosting, which we run through Decipher, Confirmit, Nebu, Sawtooth, Survey2Connect, SurveyGizmo and QuestionPro. We also have an in-house team for data tabulation, processing and analysis, along with coding, reporting and presentation. Languages: 750+ native language experts to assist clients with language and transcription needs. Data collection: Online sampling across 90+ markets; an in-house 25-seat multilingual CATI team; face-to-face and mystery shopping fieldwork across India. Qualitative: In-house moderators and recruiters for qualitative and quantitative insight. Beyond research: Software and web development, digital marketing, research consulting, and finance and accounting support such as ITR and TDS filing and GST returns.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Using the broad classifications above, from what sources of online sample do you derive participants?
faqs.a: Online proprietary panel: We actively manage our global panel (turn2opinion.com, myfrequentrewards.com and myhealthopinions.com), built through double opt-in registration where individuals voluntarily sign up and provide their demographic information to become registered members. Social media: Our recruitment team creates targeted advertisements or posts on platforms such as Facebook, LinkedIn, X and Instagram, inviting individuals to participate in our studies. Online communities: We collaborate with online communities and forums where individuals with specific interests gather, to recruit participants for our studies. Secondary customer databases: We carry out secondary research and build our own databases, inviting those contacts to our portal to take part in research studies. Partnerships and affiliations: We hold partnership pools and affiliations with other organisations, websites and communities, engaged when the need arises and after client confirmation, to reach specific demographics or niche groups.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Which of these sources are proprietary or exclusive and what is the percent share of each in the total sample provided to a buyer?
faqs.a: We use our in-house proprietary source to reach the requested audience. Whenever a shortfall arises, or the targeting is very niche, we engage our affiliates or supplier pool after client approval. On that basis, 90–95% of projects are completed with in-house sources. 90–95% of projects completed with in-house sources
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What recruitment channels are you using for each of the sources you have described? Is the recruitment process 'open to all' or by invitation only? Are you using probabilistic methods? Are you using affiliate networks and referral programs and in what proportions? How does your use of these channels vary by geography?
faqs.a: Turn2Opinion, MyFrequentRewards and MyHealthOpinions are built to recruit consumer, business and healthcare audience pools. They are recruited through traditional online sample sources, including exclusive partnerships with website publishers, social media networking platforms, online communities, and affiliate and non-profit organisation networks. Recruitment is open to all who pass the quality checks and validations applied on the portal. We do not use probabilistic methods or referral programmes. For geographic reach we keep a balance across all markets, except where the targeting required is very niche.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What form of validation do you use in recruitment to ensure that participants are real, unique, and are who they say they are?
faqs.a: We employ several validation methods during recruitment to maintain the integrity and quality of our panel database. Double opt-in: A valid email address is required at sign-up. We send a verification email requiring the participant to confirm registration via a verification link, which helps ensure the address is valid and belongs to a real person. Identity verification: We confirm participant identity, which can involve additional information such as name, address, phone number, or government-issued identification in the case of payment errors or mismatched information. These measures help prevent fraudulent or duplicate registrations. Screening questions: At registration and before each study we include screening questions covering demographics, purchasing habits, product usage and other relevant factors, so participants fit the desired target audience. Quality control: We check for inconsistent or contradictory answers using a quality score on open-ended and red-herring questions to prevent bot fraud, monitor response times, and identify patterns that suggest unreliable or careless participation. Redundancy checks: We compare participant data such as name, email address and IP address to identify multiple registrations from the same individual. Project and sample management platform: Our in-house platform continuously monitors participant behaviour and detects suspicious or fraudulent activity through fraud detection algorithms, manual review and geo validation. Age validation: Each user chooses their year of birth at registration, verified against their full date of bi
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What brand (domain) and/or app are you using with proprietary sources?
faqs.a: Our proprietary sources are Turn2Opinion, MyFrequentRewards and MyHealthOpinions. The portals are accessible on all devices, and surveys can be reached through the website portal, by email, by WhatsApp, or through the member's other social channels such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X, where a survey notification can be delivered.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Which model(s) do you offer to deliver sample? Managed service, self-serve, or API integration?
faqs.a: Managed full service: We take full responsibility for the research process on behalf of the client: designing the study, selecting the target audience, programming surveys, collecting data and delivering the final results, with guidance and recommendations throughout. API integration: Clients can integrate our panel and sample resources directly into their own systems, accessing the panel's capabilities programmatically for survey invitations, data collection and sample management inside their existing workflows.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: If offering intercepts, or providing access to more than one source, what level of transparency do you offer over the composition of your sample? Do you let buyers control which sources of sample to include in their projects, and if so how? Do you have any integration mechanisms with third-party sources offered?
faqs.a: We provide information about the sources a sample is derived from whenever the client asks, and we always obtain client approval before using a supplier database. We explain our blending methodology: how sources are combined, the weighting or proportioning used, and the quality controls applied. We provide demographic breakdowns of the sample composition — age, gender, ethnicity, geographic distribution and other relevant demographics — so clients can assess alignment with their target audience. We share our validation and quality control processes, and provide panel booklets and methodology documentation covering recruitment methods, panel sources and validation, accessible through our web portal. Buyers are offered our in-house sample source that best aligns with their target audience or research objectives. API integration lets buyers access and use their preferred sample sources programmatically while using our infrastructure and tools.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Of the sample sources you have available, how would you describe the suitability of each for different research applications?
faqs.a: For product testing and recall studies we offer high respondent engagement through our proprietary panel, and we engage only users willing to participate in multiple waves of research. 50–60% recontact rate, consumer 20–30% recontact rate, B2B 10–15% recontact rate, healthcare 1–30 min survey lengths supported We have a high representation of both mobile and desktop participants, so members can access surveys and record their participation without obstacles. We do not recruit for communities and we do not run online focus groups.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Briefly describe your overall process from invitation to survey completion. What steps do you take to achieve a sample that 'looks like' the target population? What demographic quota controls, if any, do you recommend?
faqs.a: Survey invitation: Invitations go out by email, SMS or dashboard notification, with a brief description of the study, its purpose and the incentive offered. Screening and qualification: Participants answer screening questions to confirm eligibility against the criteria set for the project. Informed consent and privacy: Participants see the purpose of the study, data collection procedures, confidentiality measures and privacy considerations, and must consent before proceeding. Survey participation: Participants complete the survey online or through a registered social channel, guided through multiple-choice, open-ended or interactive questions. Data collection and quality control: Checks for inconsistent or incomplete answers, response time monitoring and attention-check questions run during the survey. Completion and submission: Participants complete the survey by responding to all required questions. Incentive fulfilment: Participants are rewarded by monetary compensation, gift cards, PayPal, UPI or another agreed form. Analysis and reporting: Where the survey is hosted by us, responses are processed, aggregated and analysed, and compiled into a report or presentation for the client. Sampling methodology: Random, stratified or quota sampling, so participants are selected in a way that reflects the target population's diversity and composition. Demographic quotas: Quotas set from the known or estimated demographics of the target population — age, gender, income, geographic location and other relevant factors. Panel recruitment and maintenance: Continuous recruitment across
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What profiling information do you hold on at least 80% of your panel members? How often is each of those data points updated? Can you supply these data points as appends to the data set? Do you collect this profiling information directly or is it supplied by a third party?
faqs.a: Profiling begins at registration with double opt-in, age and CAPTCHA validation. Once an account is set up we collect basic demographics: age, gender, ethnicity, marital status, education level, household income and occupation. Members are then funnelled into twelve deeper profiling sections covering health, food habits, interests, hobbies and recreational activities, brand preferences, product usage and shopping preferences, travel, lifestyle, parenting and technology usage such as device preference, operating system, internet usage patterns and social media usage. Each member earns 10 points for completing a profile section, against a 1,500-point redemption threshold. Contact information is verified and updated regularly. Our in-house team monitors for inactive participants, and we run periodic profiling refreshes, prompting members to update their profiles with extra points for doing so. We collect this profiling information directly — it is not supplied by a third-party dataset.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What information do you need about a project in order to provide an estimate of feasibility? What, if anything, do you do to give upper or lower boundaries around these estimates?
faqs.a: Research objectives: The purpose of the study, the target audience and the specific research questions or hypotheses. Target audience: Age range, gender distribution, geographic location and other relevant demographics. Quota and sub-quota set: The latest quota set, so the sample can be filled accordingly. Sample size: The number of participants needed, to judge whether it can be supplied within the required timeframe. Estimated incidence: Needed to understand response and conversion rates, which drive the fieldwork timeline. Survey length and complexity: Anticipated duration, number of questions and design considerations, which affect engagement and completion. Timing and fieldwork duration: Panel availability, fieldwork constraints and the required timeline. Device restriction: Device compatibility, so the right device audience is aligned to the survey. We give upper and lower boundaries from our available resources, panel capability and past experience on similar studies — for example the likelihood of achieving the required sample size or response rate on comparable projects. Where a project involves hard-to-reach or niche populations, the estimate is wider, to account for the difficulty of recruiting those segments.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What do you do if the project proves impossible for you to complete in field? Do you inform the sample buyer as to who you would use to complete the project? In such circumstances, how do you maintain and certify third party sources/sub-contractors?
faqs.a: We promptly inform the client about the challenges and limitations that make the project unfeasible, with a clear explanation of the specific reasons or constraints. We then seek client approval before engaging trusted, vetted third-party sources to achieve the required quota, and we offer alternatives: other sample sources, an adjusted research design, refined target population criteria, or a different methodology that can achieve similar insight. Where appropriate we discuss adjustments to scope, timeline or commercial terms. Third parties are assessed on reputation, track record, expertise and adherence to industry standards before any partnership. Contractual agreements set out responsibilities, quality standards, data security, regulatory compliance, participant privacy and ethical research practice. Performance and compliance are monitored through regular audits, data validation checks and performance evaluations. Partners must comply with industry standards and guidelines such as those of ESOMAR, MRS and the Insights Association.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you set limits on the amount of time a participant can be in the router before they qualify for a survey?
faqs.a: Not applicable — we do not use survey routers.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What information about a project is given to potential participants before they choose whether to take the survey or not?
faqs.a: Survey objective: The purpose of the study, including the general topic or research objective, so members understand the context. Length of interview: The estimated length, so members know the time commitment required. Incentives: The incentive or reward offered for completing the survey — cash, gift cards or another form of compensation. Privacy and data protection: That responses are kept confidential, personal information is handled securely, and participation complies with relevant privacy regulation. Opt-in consent: That participation is entirely voluntary and declining carries no negative consequence. Contact information: How to reach our support team with questions or concerns about the survey.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you allow participants to choose a survey from a selection of available surveys? If so, what are they told about each survey that helps them to make that choice?
faqs.a: Yes. Each member sees the available survey list in their account and can start a survey from that list, which shows open and closed sections. Surveys can also be reached from an email invitation or a screening message sent to their mobile or registered social platform. The objective, length of interview, incentive, privacy and data protection terms and the consent request are all shown up front, so members can decide based on their availability, interest and suitability. A survey is usually live for a week, or longer where fieldwork requires it; once closed it no longer appears.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What ability do you have to increase (or decrease) incentives being offered to potential participants during the course of a survey? If so, can this be flagged at the participant level in the dataset?
faqs.a: We can adjust incentives during the course of a survey to optimise response rates, engagement and data quality, and we can flag the incentive level at participant level in the dataset, which allows analysis of the relationship between incentive level and participant behaviour. Adjustments follow ethical guidelines: participants are treated fairly, incentives are allocated appropriately, and any change in incentive level is clearly communicated and documented.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you measure participant satisfaction at the individual project level? If so, can you provide normative data for similar projects?
faqs.a: Yes. We run a post-survey feedback mechanism in which participants rate their experience on survey length, clarity of questions, ease of completion, relevance of content and overall satisfaction. Normative data for similar projects is difficult to share, because projects vary in volume and data granularity and the comparison is rarely like for like.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you provide a debrief report about a project after it has completed? If yes, can you provide an example?
faqs.a: Yes — on request, after a project is finished, we provide a fieldwork debrief report covering: Total sample invited Response rate Drop-out rate Over-quota rate Device used IP addresses Browser information Screen resolution
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: How often can the same individual participate in a survey? How does this vary across your sample sources? What is the maximum amount of time a person may have already been taking surveys before they entered this survey? How do you manage this?
faqs.a: 3–4 surveys per week, per member 90 days exclusion on the same survey 40 min maximum survey-taking time enforced A panellist can complete the same survey only once in a 90-day period — our proprietary panels carry a 90-day exclusion by default. For partner panels, respondents can be excluded for dynamic periods of time. All our proprietary panels use the same account and user ID information to prevent duplication across panels. Where a panellist has completed one survey for a specific customer or time range, they cannot complete another for that customer or within the defined period.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What data do you maintain on individual participants such as recent participation history, date(s) of entry, source/channel? Are you able to supply buyers with a project analysis of such individual level data? Are you able to append such data points to your participant records?
faqs.a: We hold recent participation history, dates of entry, source and channel of recruitment, demographics and other profiling data. On request we provide project analysis reports with aggregated insight and statistics on participant behaviour, response rates and other project-specific metrics. Individual-level data sharing is subject to privacy and data protection considerations, so a consent agreement is signed before any such data is shared, and the buyer must request it in advance. We can append data points to participation records.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Please describe your procedures for confirmation of participant identity at the project level, as they are implemented at the point of entry to a survey or router.
faqs.a: Registration and profile verification: Demographic information and identity verification by email, phone or age verification at sign-up. Secure login credentials: Members receive secure credentials, protected by Google CAPTCHA and a security question to prevent unauthorised access. Unique participant IDs: Each participant has a unique ID used to track and identify them across projects and surveys. Account validation: Logins from an unrecognised device trigger an account validation step before the member can continue. Profiling and screening questions: Entry questions gather demographics, interests and study-specific criteria to confirm eligibility. Cookie and device identification: Used to track activity and keep identification consistent across surveys. Fraud detection and quality control: Our sample management platform analyses behaviour, response patterns and other signals to flag suspicious activity, and digital fingerprinting identifies unauthorised IP addresses, browser information and device characteristics.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Please describe your participant quality tracking, along with any health metrics you maintain on members, and how those metrics are used to invite, track, quarantine, and block people. What processes do you have in place to compare profiled and known data to in-survey responses?
faqs.a: Quality tracking: Response rates, completion rates, abandonment rates, time taken, and the open-ended answer given at the gate survey, all read as indicators of engagement and data quality. Health metrics: Profiling data, demographics, psychographics, interests and other attributes, used to target members for surveys that match their profile. Invitation and screening: Invitations are sent on profiled and known data; screening questions at the gate survey validate eligibility again before entry. Quarantine and blocking: Members engaged in suspicious or fraudulent activity, breaching panel rules, or giving inconsistent or unreliable responses are flagged, quarantined or blocked from the platform or from specific surveys. Profiled vs in-survey comparison: Profiled and known data is compared with in-survey responses; significant inconsistency triggers investigation, a request for clarification, or exclusion of the data from analysis.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: For work where you program, host, and deliver the survey data, what processes do you have in place to reduce or eliminate undesired in-survey behaviours?
faqs.a: Random responding: Attention-check questions assess engagement; failing them flags or excludes the response from analysis. Illogical or inconsistent responding: Logic checks and validation rules compare answers for internal consistency; participants are prompted to review and revise, or asked for clarification. Overuse of item non-response: Quota limits on how many times options such as 'Don't know' can be chosen, so members give a best estimate rather than defaulting. Inaccurate or inconsistent responding: Data cleaning and validation identify response bias and outliers; participants are contacted for clarification, or blocked from further participation. Incomplete responding: Completion rates are monitored; members who consistently give incomplete responses are flagged and their data excluded where necessary. Too rapid completion: Minimum time thresholds are set; completing below the threshold flags or excludes the response. Post-survey data quality checks, including cleaning and validation, run after fieldwork to catch anything the in-survey controls did not.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Please provide the link to your participant privacy notice, as well as a summary of the key concepts it addresses.
faqs.a: Frequent Research privacy policy Our privacy policy is visible on turn2opinion.com, myfrequentrewards.com and myhealthopinions.com. It is also included in the panel registration process and on survey invitations. Every new registrant must confirm acceptance of the policy and our terms and conditions before submitting their registration.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: How do you comply with key data protection laws and regulations in the jurisdictions in which you operate? How do you address consent, data breach response, cross-border transfer, and data retention? Have you appointed a data protection officer?
faqs.a: We obtain participant consent as the legal basis for processing personal data, and give participants clear information about the purposes of collection, the types of data collected and how it will be used. Participants give informed consent and may withdraw it at any time. Regulations: We comply with the GDPR in the European Union and the CCPA in the United States, using data encryption, access controls and regular security assessments. Breach response: Incident response plans detect, respond to and mitigate breaches; affected individuals and the relevant authorities are notified as required by law. Retention: Personal data is retained only as long as necessary for the purpose it was collected for, then securely deleted or anonymised. Oversight: Our external compliance officer provides guidance on data protection and other compliance issues.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: How can participants provide, manage and revise consent for the processing of their personal data? What support channels do you provide for participants?
faqs.a: After joining Turn2Opinion, MyFrequentRewards or MyHealthOpinions, participants get a My Account area from which they can manage and revise consent for the processing of their personal data. Each portal has its own support address, and the team responds to queries within 48 hours on business days. We are also working on real-time chat support so members can be assisted around the clock.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: How do you track and comply with other applicable laws and regulations, such as those that might impact the incentives paid to participants?
faqs.a: We monitor and adhere to consumer protection law, tax law, labour law and regulations specific to the research industry. When providing incentives we make sure compensation is fair and reasonable, considering the nature and duration of the activity, the effort required, and prevailing market standards. We are transparent with participants about the nature and value of incentives and any terms attached, and participants give informed consent before taking part. Internal audits monitor incentives for compliance with the relevant regulations and guidelines.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What is your approach to collecting and processing the personal data of children and young people? Do you adhere to standards and guidelines provided by ESOMAR or GRBN member associations?
faqs.a: 15 minimum age to register on our panel When collecting personal data from children or young people we ensure appropriate parental consent, verifying the parent's identity, providing clear information about data processing, and offering mechanisms for parents to review, modify or withdraw consent. We adhere to the standards and guidelines set by ESOMAR and GRBN, and comply with data protection law governing children and young people, including COPPA in the United States and the GDPR in the European Union. Privacy-by-design principles are built into our research processes and technology.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you implement 'data protection by design' in your systems and processes? If so, please describe how.
faqs.a: Yes. We collect and process only the minimum personal data necessary for the research purpose, and use anonymisation, pseudonymisation and aggregation to reduce the risk of identification. We give participants clear information about collection and processing so they can give informed consent, with user-friendly interfaces and consent mechanisms for managing their privacy preferences. Personal data is protected by encryption, access controls, firewalls and other security mechanisms, both in transit and at rest.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: What are the key elements of your information security compliance program? Please specify the frameworks or auditing procedures you comply with or certify to. Does your program include an asset-based risk assessment and internal audit process?
faqs.a: We work to recognised frameworks and certifications, including ISO 27001 for information security management, and we are verified to ISO 20252:2019. Security policies and procedures covering access control, data encryption, incident response, employee training and vendor management. Technical controls: encryption in transit and at rest, vulnerability management, intrusion detection and prevention, firewalls, and regular patching. Incident response and management procedures covering investigation, containment, mitigation, communication and recovery. A quality manager who audits, identifies areas for improvement and verifies compliance with policies and standards.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: Do you certify to or comply with a quality framework such as ISO 20252?
faqs.a: Yes. We have implemented an ISO 20252 compliant research management system and operate an integrated management system for quality. ISO 9001:2015 Quality management ISO 27001:2015 Information security ISO 20252:2019 Market, opinion and social research Certified by IAF, EIACI, DBS and UK CERT.
faqs.t: The ESOMAR 37, answered in full.

faqs.q: How do I join MyFrequentRewards?
faqs.a: Register free with an active email address, confirm your account through the verification process, then complete your profile so relevant studies can be identified for you.

faqs.q: Is membership free?
faqs.a: Yes. Membership is free, subject to the applicable terms.

faqs.q: How do I receive survey invitations?
faqs.a: Invitations are based on your profile and the research opportunities available. When a study may match your profile, you can receive an invitation by email or see it in your account.
faqs.t: MyFrequentRewards Every opinion pays.

faqs.q: Do I need to log in every day?
faqs.a: No. Invitations can arrive by email, and available opportunities are shown in your account. The number of invitations varies, so there is no fixed daily schedule.

faqs.q: How much can I earn?
faqs.a: There is no fixed amount. Rewards vary by study, eligibility, survey length, complexity and the research sponsor's requirements.

faqs.a: You can request redemption once the applicable requirements, including the minimum redemption threshold, are met. You can view the requirements that apply to you in your account.

faqs.q: How much do accounting and bookkeeping services cost?
faqs.a: Essential starts at ₹2,499/month, Growth at ₹5,999/month and Premium at ₹11,999/month, excluding applicable GST and government or third-party fees. Final scope depends on the selected package and agreed requirements.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: What is included in bookkeeping?
faqs.a: Depending on the selected plan, services may include transaction recording, income and expense categorization, general ledger maintenance, bank reconciliation, receivables and payables tracking, and agreed financial reporting.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Which accounting software do you support?
faqs.a: We can work with accounting tools the client already uses, subject to compatibility, access permissions and the agreed scope. Common tools include Tally, Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero — support for your specific setup is confirmed before work begins.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Can you organize overdue or incomplete books?
faqs.a: Yes. Historical cleanup and catch-up bookkeeping can be assessed as a separately quoted engagement based on transaction volume, documentation quality and the condition of existing records.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Does bookkeeping include GST or TDS filing?
faqs.a: No, not within the standard packages described here. These are separate services or may be included in an explicitly agreed bundle.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Is bookkeeping the same as an audit?
faqs.a: No. Bookkeeping and report preparation are distinct from statutory audit, assurance and certification. Those activities require appropriately qualified professionals where applicable.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: How many transactions can you handle?
faqs.a: The standard plans cover up to 75, 250 and 600 transactions per month respectively. Higher volumes require an assessment and tailored quotation.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Are accounting software subscriptions included?
faqs.a: No. Software subscription charges are excluded unless specifically agreed in writing.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: Can I change packages later?
faqs.a: Package changes can be discussed when business requirements change. Any change is subject to revised scope, pricing and written agreement.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: How do AI-assisted tools fit into the process?
faqs.a: Where appropriate tools are available, automation may assist with document extraction, categorization suggestions, exception identification and workflow organization. Outputs remain subject to verification and agreed review procedures.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: What do I need to provide?
faqs.a: Typically relevant bank statements, invoices, receipts, transaction details, accounting-system access where applicable, and any required clarifications. The final document checklist is agreed during onboarding.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: How do I get started?
faqs.a: Book a free 20-minute discovery consultation. We will discuss your requirements, existing records, transaction volume and reporting needs before recommending a suitable package.
faqs.t: Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Books in order. Mind at ease.

faqs.q: How much do Accounting & Finance Consulting services cost?
faqs.a: Pricing starts at ₹5,999/project for Essential, ₹17,999/project for Growth and ₹44,999/project for Premium, excluding GST, government fees and third-party fees. The appropriate plan depends on the accounting processes, reporting routines, systems and improvements being considered. New clients can book a free 20-minute discovery consultation. Any applicable offer is subject to eligibility.
faqs.t: Accounting & Finance Consulting Stronger finance. Smarter growth.

faqs.q: What does an accounting process review include?
faqs.a: An accounting process review can examine existing workflows, general ledger procedures, transaction processing, reconciliations, approval workflows, financial reporting routines, process documentation and identified improvement opportunities. The precise review depends on the selected plan, available information and agreed engagement scope.
faqs.t: Accounting & Finance Consulting Stronger finance. Smarter growth.

faqs.q: Do you implement the recommendations?
faqs.a: We can provide agreed implementation guidance, workflow documentation and monitoring support where included in the engagement. Software licensing, full ERP implementation and additional implementation work are not automatically included. Responsibilities, deliverables and any additional fees are agreed in writing before work begins.
faqs.t: Accounting & Finance Consulting Stronger finance. Smarter growth.

faqs.q: Do you replace our finance team?
faqs.a: No. Accounting & Finance Consulting supports your business by reviewing processes, identifying practical improvements and strengthening documentation and reporting routines. It does not replace your finance team or include day-to-day accounting operations. Any outsourced consulting support is defined separately in the agreed scope.
faqs.t: Accounting & Finance Consulting Stronger finance. Smarter growth.

faqs.q: Is legal or statutory audit work included?
faqs.a: No. This service does not include legal advice, statutory audit, independent audit opinions or certification. It focuses on accounting and finance process consulting, reporting workflows, operational improvements and related agreed support.
faqs.t: Accounting & Finance Consulting Stronger finance. Smarter growth.

faqs.q: How much do Audit & Compliance Support services cost?
faqs.a: Plans start at ₹7,999/project for Essential, ₹19,999/project for Growth and ₹44,999/project for Premium. Prices exclude GST, government fees and third-party fees. A free 20-minute discovery consultation is available to new clients. Other offers are subject to their eligibility conditions and the proposal.
faqs.t: Audit & Compliance Support Audit-ready, every single day.

faqs.q: Do you perform statutory audits?
faqs.a: No. This service provides audit-readiness, documentation, reconciliation, internal-control documentation, compliance tracking and audit-coordination support within the agreed scope. It does not include statutory audits, independent audit opinions, certifications or assurance engagements. Where a statutory audit or regulated professional service is required, it must be performed by an appropriately qualified and authorised professional.
faqs.t: Audit & Compliance Support Audit-ready, every single day.

faqs.q: What does an audit-readiness review cover?
faqs.a: An audit-readiness review may cover the availability of accounting records, financial statement schedules, reconciliation status, supporting documentation, internal-control records, evidence organisation, identified documentation gaps and management action plans. The precise review depends on the selected plan, available records and agreed engagement scope.
faqs.t: Audit & Compliance Support Audit-ready, every single day.

faqs.q: Can you coordinate with our auditor?
faqs.a: Yes. Audit-related coordination and organisation of requested information can be included where agreed. This may involve organising supporting schedules, tracking information requests and recording follow-up items. Your appointed auditor remains responsible for their independent audit work, professional judgements and conclusions.
faqs.t: Audit & Compliance Support Audit-ready, every single day.

faqs.q: Is historical cleanup included?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The listed plans cover defined record assessments, reviews, schedules and documentation deliverables. Extensive historical bookkeeping, transaction corrections, reconstruction of missing records or additional reconciliation work may require separate scoping and quotation. The exact inclusions are confirmed before work begins.
faqs.t: Audit & Compliance Support Audit-ready, every single day.

faqs.q: How much does Budgeting & Financial Forecasting cost?
faqs.a: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting is quoted according to the agreed scope, including the number of entities and departments, model depth and forecast-update frequency. You receive a written quotation before work begins. The service is also included within the Financial Planning & Advisory and Virtual CFO offerings, subject to each plan's scope. Prices exclude GST.
faqs.t: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting Plan for every possible future.

faqs.q: What is a rolling forecast?
faqs.a: A rolling forecast is a financial projection that is reviewed and updated periodically as new information becomes available. Rather than relying only on a budget prepared once a year, it helps management revisit assumptions and extend the planning horizon. The update frequency and deliverables depend on the agreed engagement.
faqs.t: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting Plan for every possible future.

faqs.q: How is pricing set for budgeting work?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the business structure, number of entities and departments, required model detail, available historical data, scenario requirements and how frequently forecasts need updating. We discuss these requirements during the discovery consultation and provide a written quotation before work starts.
faqs.t: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting Plan for every possible future.

faqs.q: Can you build a three-statement forecast?
faqs.a: An integrated three-statement forecast can be discussed where the engagement requires projected profit and loss, balance sheet and cash-flow statements. The model depends on the availability and quality of historical financial information, documented assumptions and the agreed scope. The required outputs and modelling boundaries are confirmed before work begins.
faqs.t: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting Plan for every possible future.

faqs.q: Will the forecast be accurate?
faqs.a: A forecast is an estimate based on assumptions and information available at the time it is prepared. Actual results may differ as sales, costs, collections, market conditions and business decisions change. We focus on making assumptions explicit, documenting scenarios and supporting agreed updates. We do not guarantee that projected results will match actual performance.
faqs.t: Budgeting & Financial Forecasting Plan for every possible future.

A free 20-minute discovery consultation is available to new clients. Eligible offers may apply subject to the proposal and applicable conditions.

faqs.q: Do you arrange loans or act as a broker?

faqs.t: Business Finance Services Finance that fuels your next step.

faqs.q: What does a funding-readiness review cover?

Final pricing is confirmed after a scoping call based on the corporate finance question, financial information available, modelling complexity and number of scenarios. A free 20-minute discovery consultation is available to new clients. Offers are subject to eligibility.

faqs.q: Do you provide registered or certified valuations?

If your transaction or legal requirements call for a valuation by a registered or otherwise authorised professional, that work must be undertaken by an appropriately qualified and authorised provider.
faqs.t: Corporate Finance Advisory Capital decisions, made with confidence.

faqs.q: Do you execute transactions or raise funds?

faqs.q: Can you build a corporate financial model?

faqs.t: Corporate Finance Advisory Capital decisions, made with confidence.

faqs.q: Why are the prices listed as 'starting from'?
faqs.a: Corporate finance projects differ in complexity, data availability, modelling requirements, number of scenarios, management deliverables and transaction context. After a scoping call, the proposal confirms the agreed analysis, assumptions, deliverables, timeline and final fee.
faqs.t: Corporate Finance Advisory Capital decisions, made with confidence.

faqs.q: What is B2B digital marketing?

faqs.q: How is your approach to B2B marketing different?
faqs.a: It starts with buyer intelligence — industries, company types, roles, decision influence, information needs and buying stage — and builds positioning, content, channels and measurement around the buying committee rather than a single lead.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: Do you have data on every company or market?
faqs.a: No. The work uses the account, CRM and intent sources available to you and the platforms involved. No access to verified data on every market or company is claimed.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: What's the difference between demand generation and lead generation?
faqs.a: Demand generation builds awareness and preference before buyers are ready; lead generation captures identifiable interest when they are. B2B growth usually needs both.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: Do you support account-based marketing?
faqs.a: Yes — account prioritisation, buying-group mapping, personalised content and account-level engagement, aligned with sales.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: How does AI support B2B marketing?
faqs.a: AI helps with account clustering, market-signal summaries, content variations, campaign analysis and reporting. Strategy, interpretation and final decisions stay human-led.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: How long does B2B marketing take to generate results?
faqs.a: It depends on your market, sales cycle, starting point and investment. Realistic milestones are set rather than guarantees.
faqs.t: B2B Digital Marketing Reach the buyers who sign the deals.

faqs.q: How do you decide what content to create?
faqs.a: We start from the questions your buyers ask at each stage — from search data, sales conversations, support queries and competitor gaps — then decide which questions are worth answering and in what format.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: What types of content do you produce?
faqs.a: Articles, guides, service and landing-page copy, comparison pages, checklists, whitepapers, social content, email content and video scripts — chosen by what the question needs.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: Can you improve the content we already have?
faqs.a: Yes. A content audit shows what to keep, refresh, merge or retire. Improving existing pages is often faster than publishing new ones.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: How do you keep content on-brand and accurate?
faqs.a: Every piece goes through editorial review for accuracy, originality, readability and brand voice before it is published.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: How do you use AI in content marketing?
faqs.a: AI helps cluster questions, explore topics, draft outlines, summarise sources and repurpose formats. Strategy, writing quality, fact-checking, brand voice and approval stay with people.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: How do you measure content?
faqs.a: By what it changes: visibility for the right questions, engaged time, return visits, sign-ups, enquiries and assisted conversions — not just page views.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: How long does content take to work?
faqs.a: Distributed content can work within days; search-driven content usually builds over months. We plan both so the programme isn't waiting on one channel.
faqs.t: Content Marketing Stories that rank, engage and convert.

faqs.q: What is digital marketing consulting?
faqs.a: Independent, business-first advice that helps you make a marketing decision — where to focus, which audiences matter, which channels play which role, how to measure and how to invest — and turns it into a practical roadmap.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: How is your approach to consulting different?
faqs.a: Advice starts from the business question and evidence — audience, market, performance and customer data — rather than from the channels a provider happens to sell. Options are compared openly, and recommendations come with the evidence behind them.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: When should a business hire a digital marketing consultant?
faqs.a: When marketing feels fragmented, spend isn't clearly linked to results, you're entering a new market, choosing between strategic options or need a roadmap before scaling activity.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: Do you provide a strategy or only recommendations?
faqs.a: Both: a diagnosis, strategic options, a priority matrix, a measurement framework and a roadmap — and, if you want, help activating it through the digital marketing services.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: Can you help us decide which channels to prioritise?
faqs.a: Yes. Each channel's role is assessed against your audience, business model, maturity and objective — the right mix differs for every business.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: How does AI support consulting?
faqs.a: AI speeds up analysis, scenario comparison, pattern detection and summarisation. People make the strategic decisions and validate every recommendation.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee marketing results?
faqs.a: No. Rankings, ROAS or revenue aren't guaranteed — the work provides clear priorities, honest evidence and a practical plan.
faqs.t: Digital Marketing Consulting A growth plan built on evidence.

faqs.q: What is e-commerce marketing?
faqs.a: E-commerce marketing brings the right shoppers to an online store, helps them find and choose products, removes friction to purchase and encourages them to come back — across search, shopping, social, email, WhatsApp and the store itself.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: How is your approach to e-commerce different?
faqs.a: It looks at the whole customer journey, not just the click: segments, category understanding, product discovery, purchase barriers, behaviour, conversion signals and repeat purchase. Decisions are judged against the real economics where data allows.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: What does an e-commerce marketing service include?
faqs.a: Depending on your needs: strategy, e-commerce SEO, shopping and search ads, product feed optimisation, social advertising, product page and checkout optimisation, email and WhatsApp retention, analytics and reporting.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: Which platforms do you work with?
faqs.a: Common store platforms such as Shopify, WooCommerce and Magento, and marketplaces where relevant. No official platform partnerships are claimed.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee more sales?
faqs.a: No. Sales depend on product, pricing, competition, stock, budget and the store experience. The work improves the evidence behind every decision; outcomes are never guaranteed.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: How does AI support e-commerce marketing?
faqs.a: AI can help with product description drafts, feed enrichment, segmentation, behaviour pattern detection and performance summaries. People decide pricing, offers, brand presentation and what goes live.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: How do you measure e-commerce marketing?
faqs.a: Beyond revenue: conversion by stage, average order value, repeat purchase, customer value and — where data allows — contribution after advertising, discounts, fulfilment and returns.
faqs.t: E-commerce Marketing More carts. Fewer abandons.

faqs.q: What makes your email marketing different?
faqs.a: We run email as lifecycle communication, not a send calendar. Behaviour — what people open, click, buy or ignore — decides the next message, and every journey is measured by what it moves forward.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: Can you work with our existing email platform and CRM?
faqs.a: Yes. We work in the platforms you already use where they support the journeys you need, and improve how the CRM, website and email tool share data.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: Do you use purchased lists?
faqs.a: No. We work only with permission-based, first-party contacts. It protects deliverability, your reputation and your customers' trust.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: How do you use AI in email marketing?
faqs.a: AI helps with subject-line ideas, content variations, segment suggestions and spotting which signals predict action or churn. People decide the journeys, the voice, the compliance and what gets sent.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: How do you measure email?
faqs.a: Beyond opens: clicks, replies, website actions, conversions, journey progression, retention and unsubscribes — matched to what each journey is meant to do.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee inbox placement?
faqs.a: No one can. We improve the odds through list hygiene, consent-aware sending, authentication and engagement-based practices.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.q: Can email work for B2B as well as e-commerce?
faqs.a: Yes. B2B journeys nurture longer, multi-person decisions; e-commerce journeys handle welcome, browse, cart, post-purchase and win-back moments.
faqs.t: Email Marketing Inbox moments people actually open.

faqs.a: The journey is understood before anything is automated: who the customers are, what signals show intent, which lifecycle stage they're in, what consent allows and what the business rules are. Automation without strategy simply creates more messages.
faqs.t: Marketing Automation The right message, at the right moment, automatically.

faqs.a: Depending on your needs: strategy, CRM workflows, email automation, lead nurturing, segmentation, lead scoring, integrations, reporting and ongoing optimisation.

faqs.q: What is online reputation management?
faqs.a: Online reputation management (ORM) is monitoring, understanding and influencing how a brand is represented and perceived across the online channels that matter to its customers — search results, reviews, social media, forums and news.

faqs.a: It's our starting point for reputation work: understanding what people say, how they feel, which themes recur, where risk is building and what customers expect — before deciding what to say back.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: What does an online reputation management service include?
faqs.a: Depending on your needs: monitoring, review management, sentiment and theme analysis, response strategy, escalation processes, search reputation, trust-building content and reporting.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: Can you remove negative reviews?
faqs.a: No promise of removal is made. Legitimate reviews generally can't simply be removed. The work focuses on appropriate responses, resolving issues where possible, reporting content that breaks a platform's own policies, and strengthening credible information.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee search results or ratings?
faqs.a: No. Search results, rankings and ratings depend on platforms and on what people write, so no specific outcome is guaranteed.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: How does AI support reputation management?
faqs.a: AI can help classify mentions by sentiment and theme, summarise conversations and detect patterns. People review sensitive responses, judge context and decide on escalation.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: How much does online reputation management cost?
faqs.a: It depends on scope, markets, channels, monitoring requirements and complexity, so an assessment usually comes first.
faqs.t: Online Reputation Management Be the brand people recommend.

faqs.q: How does IT consulting reduce technology investment risk?
faqs.a: By testing options against business goals, existing systems, integration, security, cost and team capability before you commit — so expensive surprises surface on paper, not in production.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: Can you review our existing technology architecture?
faqs.a: Yes. An architecture review covers applications, integrations, data, cloud, security and technical debt, with prioritised recommendations.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: Do you create IT strategies and technology roadmaps?
faqs.a: Yes — roadmaps that say what to do now, next and later, with the reasoning, dependencies and investment priorities behind each step.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: Can you identify practical AI and automation opportunities?
faqs.a: Yes. We look for workflows where AI or automation clearly reduces effort or improves decisions, and say plainly where traditional software is the better answer.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: Can you advise on build versus buy?
faqs.a: Yes. We compare building, buying and hybrid options on fit, differentiation, integration, speed and total cost of ownership.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: Can your consultants work with our existing IT or development team?
faqs.a: Yes. We can advise alongside your team, review their plans or take on delivery, depending on what you need.
faqs.t: IT Consulting Technology decisions, made with clarity.

faqs.q: When does a business actually need a mobile app?
faqs.a: When people need to do something repeatedly, on the move, at a specific moment — check in, capture, track, order, approve — or when device capabilities such as notifications, camera, location or offline access genuinely matter. If use is occasional and mostly reading, a responsive website or web app may be enough.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: Can a mobile app connect to an existing backend?
faqs.a: Yes. Apps can use existing APIs and systems — CRM, ERP, payment, booking and others — or new APIs can be built where the backend doesn't yet expose what the app needs.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: How do you approach offline functionality?
faqs.a: Only where the use case needs it. Offline-first design stores data locally, queues changes on the device and syncs when a connection returns, with clear rules for conflicts. It is planned from the start because it is hard to add later.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: Can the same product support web and mobile experiences?
faqs.a: Yes. A shared backend and API can serve a web application and mobile apps, each designed for how people use that device, so business logic and data stay consistent.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: Should I choose native or cross-platform?
faqs.a: Cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter or React Native suit many business apps and share one codebase. Native development suits apps that rely heavily on device hardware, complex graphics or platform-specific behaviour.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee app store approval?
faqs.a: No one can — Apple and Google make those decisions. Apps are built to their published guidelines and submissions are prepared carefully to reduce the risk of rejection.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: How much does mobile app development cost?
faqs.a: It depends on platforms, screens, features, integrations, offline needs, security and support, so an estimate follows discovery rather than a generic price.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: Who owns the app and source code?
faqs.a: Ownership depends on the project agreement. It is recommended that your organisation holds the app store developer accounts and agrees code ownership upfront.
faqs.t: Mobile App Development Apps people keep on their home screen.

faqs.q: What should a SaaS MVP include?
faqs.a: The smallest product that proves the core value for a defined set of users: the main workflow, sign-up and authentication, basic roles, the data model, essential admin tools and enough analytics to learn from usage. Billing, integrations and advanced features follow once the core is validated — but the architecture should not block them.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: How should multi-tenancy be designed?
faqs.a: Around how customers' data must be separated, how much customisation each tenant needs, compliance expectations and expected scale. Shared databases with tenant isolation, separate schemas or separate databases each have trade-offs in cost, security and operational effort, so the choice is made per product.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: Can SaaS support subscription and usage-based models?
faqs.a: Yes. Plans, feature entitlements, trials, seats, usage metering, invoicing and payment-provider integration can be designed so pricing can change without rebuilding the product.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: How can AI be incorporated into a SaaS product?
faqs.a: Where it creates value for users: assistants that help complete tasks, semantic search, recommendations, workflow automation, natural-language analytics and intelligent alerts — designed to be purposeful, permissioned, governed and observable.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: How should a SaaS product evolve after launch?
faqs.a: Through a steady loop of observing usage, learning from customers, prioritising and releasing improvements — supported by product analytics, observability, feature flags and a roadmap that balances new features with reliability and technical health.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: Which technologies are used for SaaS products?
faqs.a: The stack follows the requirement. Common choices include React or Next.js on the front end, Node.js, PHP / Laravel or Python on the back end, and AWS, Azure or Google Cloud for infrastructure — without implying every product uses every technology.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: How much does SaaS development cost?
faqs.a: It depends on scope, tenancy model, integrations, billing complexity, AI features, security requirements and support, so an estimate follows discovery rather than a generic price.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: Who owns the SaaS product and code?
faqs.a: Ownership of code, IP and accounts is set out in the project agreement and is best agreed before development begins.
faqs.t: SaaS Development From idea to subscription-ready product.

faqs.q: What does your Software Testing & QA service include?

faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.a: Yes. Automation covers repeatable checks; experienced testers focus on judgement, exploration and the journeys where mistakes are expensive.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: Can you test an existing website or application?
faqs.a: Yes — including software built by another team. We start by mapping critical journeys and the areas of highest risk.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: Can you build automated regression testing into our pipeline?
faqs.a: Yes. Automated web and API suites can run in your CI/CD pipeline on every change and report clearly when something breaks.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: Can you test APIs and third-party integrations?
faqs.a: Yes — behaviour, contracts, authentication, error responses, data consistency and edge cases across the connected systems.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: How is AI used in software testing?
faqs.a: AI assists with scenario discovery, test-data generation, failure clustering, flaky-test detection and result summaries; engineers validate what matters before anything ships.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: Do you provide performance testing?
faqs.a: Yes — load, stress and scalability testing that shows how the system behaves as users and traffic grow, before your customers find out.
faqs.t: Software Testing & QA Catch the bug before your users do.

faqs.q: Can QA continue throughout ongoing development?
faqs.a: Yes. Continuous testing can run alongside every sprint and release rather than as a phase at the end.

faqs.q: What does your UI/UX Design service include?
faqs.a: UX strategy, user journeys, information architecture, wireframes, prototypes, UI design, design systems, accessibility and developer handoff — scoped to the product and the problem.

faqs.q: What is the difference between UI and UX design?
faqs.a: UX design shapes how a product works — the path, structure and interactions that help people reach a goal; UI design shapes how it looks and feels on screen. Good products need both working together.
faqs.t: UI/UX Design Complex products that feel simple.

faqs.q: Can you redesign an existing website or application?
faqs.a: Yes. We usually start with a UX review to find where users struggle, then redesign the paths, structure and interface that matter most.
faqs.t: UI/UX Design Complex products that feel simple.

faqs.q: Can you design UX for complex business software?
faqs.a: Yes — dashboards, ERP and CRM interfaces, admin tools, approval systems and other information-heavy products, designed around roles, priorities and real tasks.
faqs.t: UI/UX Design Complex products that feel simple.

faqs.q: Do you design mobile applications?
faqs.a: Yes — iOS, Android and cross-platform experiences designed for the context of use, not simply a shrunken desktop layout.
faqs.t: UI/UX Design Complex products that feel simple.

faqs.q: Can you design AI-powered product experiences?
faqs.a: Yes — assistants, AI search, recommendations and human-in-the-loop workflows designed for transparency, control and useful outcomes.
faqs.t: UI/UX Design Complex products that feel simple.

faqs.q: When should a business build a web application?
faqs.a: When important work depends on spreadsheets, email threads, manual approvals or disconnected tools — and the business needs the same process to run reliably for more people, with clear roles, rules and visibility. If an existing product already fits the workflow, buying or extending it may be the better route.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: Can existing workflows be converted into a digital application?
faqs.a: Yes — but the opportunity is not simply to digitise them. The workflow is mapped first: who does what, which rules apply, where approvals sit and what data is needed. Then the application is designed around how the work should happen.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: Can a web application integrate with existing systems?
faqs.a: Yes, using the supported APIs of CRM, ERP, payment, identity, communication or analytics systems, or agreed data-exchange methods such as webhooks, scheduled imports or queues.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: How are roles and permissions handled?
faqs.a: Roles are defined around real responsibilities — admin, manager, operator, customer, partner, approver — and each sees only the screens, data and actions they need. Every request passes through authentication and permission checks, and important actions can be logged.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a website and a web application?
faqs.a: A website helps people discover and understand a business. A web application helps them do something — submit, approve, track, book, analyse — usually behind a login.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: Will a web application work on mobile?
faqs.a: Responsive design makes it usable in mobile browsers. If offline use or device features matter, a mobile app or progressive web app can be considered.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build a web application?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. Many projects start with the core workflow, then grow in planned releases as usage shows what matters next.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: How much does web application development cost?
faqs.a: It depends on users and roles, workflows, integrations, data, security and support, so an estimate follows discovery rather than a generic price.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: Who owns the source code?
faqs.a: Ownership of source code and IP depends on the project agreement, and is best agreed clearly before development begins.
faqs.t: Web Application Development Powerful web apps, delightfully fast.

faqs.q: How should a business website connect with CRM, analytics or other systems?
faqs.a: Start from what should happen after a visitor acts: where an enquiry goes, who follows up and what needs measuring. Forms, CRM, booking, payments, analytics and marketing tools are then connected through their supported APIs or integrations, so the website feeds the business instead of creating another inbox.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: How do you approach performance and accessibility?
faqs.a: Both are designed in, not checked at the end: optimised images, efficient JavaScript, caching and Core Web Vitals considerations for performance, and WCAG-conscious design — keyboard access, contrast, focus states, accessible forms — for accessibility. Specific scores are never promised before they are measured.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: Can an existing website be modernised instead of rebuilt?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If the platform and content structure are sound, a redesign, performance work or new integrations may achieve more than a rebuild. A rebuild makes sense when the platform itself limits what the business needs.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: Can you redesign my website without losing search visibility?
faqs.a: A redesign should protect what already works: existing URLs are mapped, 301 redirects planned, metadata preserved and search performance monitored after launch.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: How should a website be prepared for future functionality?
faqs.a: By choosing a CMS and architecture that fit today's needs while leaving room for what is likely next — e-commerce, portals, integrations or AI-assisted search — without over-engineering for features that may never be needed.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: Should I choose WordPress, Shopify or custom development?
faqs.a: It depends on what the website must do. WordPress suits content-led sites that are edited often, Shopify suits product catalogues and online selling, and custom development suits unusual workflows, integrations or performance needs.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: Where can AI genuinely add value on a website?
faqs.a: Intelligent search, content assistance for editors, support journeys and analytics insights are common candidates. Each AI feature is planned with clear data boundaries and human review.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: How much does website development cost?
faqs.a: Cost depends on templates, custom functionality, CMS, integrations, content, languages and support needs, so a scoped estimate follows a short discovery rather than a generic price list.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.

faqs.q: Who owns the website after launch?
faqs.a: Ownership of code, content, domains and accounts is set out in the project agreement. Holding your own domain, hosting and key accounts is recommended.
faqs.t: Website Development Websites that work as hard as you do.
