faqs.q: What is a Business Panel?
faqs.a: A business panel is a community of verified professionals who have agreed to take part in research and shared details about their role, company and industry. It lets research teams reach the right B2B respondents quickly instead of recruiting from scratch for every study.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: What types of business professionals can you recruit?
faqs.a: Our business panel includes 2.85M+ verified business professionals, including decision-makers, influencers, key stakeholders, C-suite professionals, senior managers, SME owners, function-specific professionals and IT and technology decision-makers.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: Can I target respondents by industry and job role?
faqs.a: Yes. Industry, job role, department and seniority are core profiling attributes, and they can be combined with company attributes such as employee size, revenue and organization type.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: Can Business Panel research target senior decision-makers?
faqs.a: Yes. The panel includes C-suite professionals and senior managers. Because senior audiences are harder to reach, we confirm feasibility for your specific criteria and markets before fieldwork starts.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: What company-level attributes can be used for B2B targeting?
faqs.a: Industry, sector, employee size, company revenue, organization type and company location, alongside market-level attributes such as country and region.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: Which markets can you cover?
faqs.a: We run B2B research across 55+ markets. Share your target countries and we will confirm coverage and feasibility for each one.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: How do you maintain Business Panel data quality?
faqs.a: Depending on study requirements, we apply identity and access checks such as CAPTCHA and security questions, fraud prevention such as duplicate, bot and TOR detection, and research-quality checks such as screening filters, open-end reviews and red-herring questions.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: How quickly can you assess B2B sample feasibility?
faqs.a: For most studies we share feasibility and a cost estimate within one working day. Complex or very senior audiences can take a little longer because we check real availability first.
faqs.t: Business Panel Decision-makers, verified and ready to answer.

faqs.q: What is CATI research?
faqs.a: CATI (computer-assisted telephone interviewing) is telephone research in which interviewers follow a structured questionnaire on screen and record answers directly into the CATI system as the interview happens.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: What types of respondents can you interview through CATI?
faqs.a: We interview consumers (B2C), business professionals and decision-makers (B2B), and healthcare audiences such as physicians, pharmacists, nurses, patients and caregivers. Availability for each audience is confirmed per country during feasibility.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Can you conduct multilingual CATI studies?
faqs.a: Yes. Our multilingual interviewers support studies across the Americas, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East, with native-language interviewing arranged where the project requires it.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Can CATI interviews be recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Audio or video recordings can be made when the client or project requires them.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Do you conduct back checks?
faqs.a: Yes. Back checks and respondent authentication are carried out according to project requirements, with coverage agreed per study within a range of 30% to 100% of interviews.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Can you handle difficult-to-reach B2B and healthcare audiences?
faqs.a: Yes. Our experience includes CXOs, directors, senior and middle management, procurement professionals, physician specialists, surgeons, pharmacists and patient audiences.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Do you provide 24/7 CATI support?
faqs.a: Our CATI operation is set up for round-the-clock availability, so calling can be scheduled for respondents in different time zones. Shift plans are agreed for each project.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: Can CATI be combined with other research methods?
faqs.a: Yes. CATI can sit alongside online research, in-depth interviews, focus groups, face-to-face interviews, mystery shopping and secondary research within one programme.
faqs.t: CATI — Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing Real voices. Every call quality-checked.

faqs.q: What is offline data collection?
faqs.a: Offline data collection gathers research data through direct contact with respondents, such as face-to-face interviews, rather than through self-completed online surveys.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: What is CAPI?
faqs.a: CAPI (computer-assisted personal interviewing) is face-to-face interviewing on a tablet or mobile device, with routing and skip logic programmed into the questionnaire and answers captured digitally.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: What is PAPI?
faqs.a: PAPI (paper-assisted personal interviewing) uses printed questionnaires, for field environments where digital collection may not be practical.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: When should I use face-to-face data collection?
faqs.a: It suits audiences who are hard to reach online, longer or more involved questionnaires, product or concept testing, and studies that benefit from direct interaction.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: Can you conduct face-to-face research in rural areas?
faqs.a: Yes. Rural and semi-urban fieldwork can be supported depending on the audience, geography and feasibility.

faqs.q: Can you conduct B2B and healthcare face-to-face interviews?
faqs.a: Yes. We conduct face-to-face interviews with business and professional audiences and with healthcare audiences, subject to feasibility.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: How do you maintain fieldwork quality?
faqs.a: Through respondent screening, interviewer training, supervisor monitoring, back checks and data validation, with GPS, time and duration checks where applicable.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: Can face-to-face data collection use tablets?
faqs.a: Yes. CAPI uses tablets or mobile devices with programmed digital questionnaires, which supports real-time capture and field monitoring.
faqs.t: Offline Data Collection Face to face, wherever your audience lives.

faqs.q: What is research design?
faqs.a: Research design is the plan that connects a business question to the evidence needed to answer it: the objectives, audience, sample, methodology, data collection and analysis approach.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: Why is research design important?
faqs.a: Most research problems start before fieldwork. A clear design keeps objectives, sample, methodology and analysis aligned, so the findings can support a real decision.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: What does a research design process include?
faqs.a: Our research design cycle has seven stages: understand, define the framework, design the methodology, execute fieldwork, analyse, validate and recommend, with learning that feeds the next question.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: How do you choose between qualitative and quantitative research?
faqs.a: Qualitative research suits exploring motivations, perceptions and language; quantitative research suits measuring, comparing and sizing. Many projects combine both in a mixed-method design.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: What is the difference between research design and research methodology?
faqs.a: Research design is the overall plan for answering the question. Research methodology is the set of methods used within that plan, such as surveys, interviews or focus groups.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: How does Frequent Research manage research quality?
faqs.a: Quality is built in at every stage: clear objectives in design, relevant audiences in sampling, monitoring during fieldwork, cleaning and validation of data, consistency checks in analysis and internal review before delivery.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: Can Frequent Research conduct multi-market research?
faqs.a: Yes. We design and run single-market and multi-market studies across 55+ markets, with consistent screening and quality controls.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.

faqs.q: Can you design a research methodology around a specific business question?
faqs.a: Yes. Every design starts from the decision you need to make, and the methodology, audience and sample are chosen to answer it.
faqs.t: Research Design Cycle Seven steps from brief to decision.
